recipes.name: Cheesy Chicken Meatballs
ingredients_raw: 0.25 cup roasted garlic light cream cheese

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). Line a rimmed baking sheet with aluminum foil, and spray with cooking spray.

Combine the chicken, eggs, cream cheese, Parmesan cheese, bread crumbs, red pepper flakes, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, vegetable oil, salt, and pepper in a large bowl; mix well. Form mixture into 20 meatballs; place on prepared pan.
Bake in center of preheated oven until juices run clear, 17 to 18 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Cheesy Chicken Meatballs
raw_recipe.description: Garlic cream cheese adds great flavor to these zesty chicken meatballs, while ensuring that they'll be light, moist, and delicious.

review.reviewBody: EDIT- You can reduce to 1 egg - I was doubling this recipe from my original to serve more people but realized the 2 eggs is probably a bit much - would be fine with 1 for those having trouble making balls out of them. It's hard in the beginning but they result in a moist meatball. :)Also, you can add more breadcrumbs to balance out the moistness if you are having trouble. AND I just noticed in the directions/ingredients, that oil is added to the mixture - I don't add any oil to this mixture - I only spray the baking sheet with oil. :S

So delicious! I doubled the recipe. The made two changes. One was with the cream cheese. My surrounding grocery stores didn't have garlic cream cheese so I used herbs and spices cream cheese and it was wonderful. The other change was not only did I bake them but I also fried some. These meatballs were so flavorful I will be making these many more times!! My boys loved them as well.

They were awesome.. Did make twicks, as others said. 1 egg, used 1 T Italian bread crumbs, Added 1/2 T Italian seasoning..added some chopped onions. NO oil, sprayed foil on baking sheet. Used everything else in recipe. Would have added mozz too, didn't have any 🤪 Baked 400 and turned 1/2 way thru. Heated jar of alfredo in skillet and added meatballs to heat thru with sauce. Cooked egg noodles and topped with the meat balls and sauce when drained noodles. Had a nice loaf of Itailian bread with butter and garlic in the brolier.. Bon appetit'

These little nuggets were really delicious! I made them exactly according to the recipe except leaving out one egg and leaving out the salt. They were a little sticky to roll so they were meat lumps 😏. I have never cooked with red pepper flakes, but they added a little bit of heat without overpowering the chicken flavors. I will make it again, maybe with more bread crumbs. I served it with Alfredo sauce on rotini, but I could have left out the pasta, they were that good. I have also made them now in a frying pan, seared, then cooked with cream of mushroom soup in low heat, served on mashed potatoes. Still a keeper!

I will make these again! I followed the update and added only the one egg and a bit more bread crumbs. I liked the idea of another reviewer and added Laughing Cow Garlic and Herb wedges(2) instead of the cream cheese. I added the oil this time but may omit next time around. They were very moist and on the soft side. I will omit oil next time and see if I prefer the consistency. Also want to thank same reviewer for tip of spraying olive oil spray onto my hands to roll up the meatballs. It worked like a charm. The meatballs were spicy in a good way. My husband approved!!

Great recipe. I can't always find the roasted garlic cream cheese so I just add plain cream cheese and some minced garlic. I've made these as the meatballs added to sauce for spaghetti and meatballs. I've also made patties and created a Greek type meal with tzatziki, pita and potatoes. The other night I made small patties and made a pan gravy. I have cooked these in the oven and pan fried them simply by spraying my frying pan with cooking spray. All depends if my oven is free :) These are so tasty. Great recipe Raquel

These were so good ! I read some reviews and took the advice of others.. I used 1 egg per 1 pound of chicken (but doubled it so 2 & 2).. no oil, and did 1/4 cup cream cheese and 1/4 cup feta. They held up well and cooked evenly and hopefully will feed the family for more than one meal !

Hosting a grain free baby shower and thought I'd try these out to stay in the healthy zone. Substituted almond flour for the bread crumbs and since I didn't read the reviews used two eggs which made things gloppy. Added about 2 more Tbsps almond flour and used my cookie scoop with spring mechanism which worked great. Made 35 smalls balls, baked 15mins. Used Laughing Cow Swiss since didn't have cream cheese. Served with homemade barbecue sauce. Excellent. By themselves the seasoning seemed a bit strong, but with the sauce it was fine.

This was a great recipe!! I didn't follow it to a T but I used it as a base. Here are the modifications I made. I used 1 egg, olive oil in place of vegetable, instead of 1 TBSP garlic powder I only used 1 tsp garlic powder and added about 4 gloves of fresh garlic (grated). I also used plain low fat cream cheese, because I couldn't find the garlic roasted one. And instead of Italian seasoning (because I didn't have any) I used fresh basil (about 2 tsp), 1/2 tsp dried parsley, and 1/2 tsp dried oregano. I got about 12 meatball from this because I made them pretty big, and I stuffed fresh mozzarella cheese in 1/2 of them. I also used an ice cream scoop and a spoon to form the balls - to keep hands clean and get them rounded pretty good!. I baked them on 425 for about 25 minutes (my fire alarm usually goes off if my oven is over 400 so I'm surprised I was able to get it to 425). Then I threw them in my pot of marinara sauce for about 10 minutes. They were amazing! Definitely a keeper! Thank you for sharing!

I did tweek alot! After reading all the reviews I added only one egg, 3/4 Tbls oil, 1/4 tsp cayenne (No red pepper but I'll add 1/2 tsp cayenne next time), no salt (parmesan cheese is already salty), and the rest of the spices as written. I also added 1/3 cup mozzarella to the mix. They were still pretty soft when I plopped on the baking sheet, but stayed in ball shape. I also sprinkled parm on top before baking. (We are a VERY cheesy family 😉). I also lowered the temp. Got 25 luscious, delicious, and moist chicken meat-a-balls. Served in Alfredo sauce. They were a huge hit! Chef's kiss worthy!

Excellent results. I made these into chicken burgers. Using wet hands shape into 3.5" diameter patties. Then pan fry a few minutes each side on a lightly oiled non-stick skillet. Serve on warm burger buns and dinner is served.
Love It
Excellent family loved it!

Hubs loved these! Made half a batch, no egg or oil as they were pretty sticky as is. Used regular cream cheese and roasted fresh garlic because I have never seen garlic cream cheese. Added more lemon panko vs bread crumbs till they formed a nice texture. Let the mixture rest about thirty minutes before shaping and baking. These can be served in so many ways! Tonight was over pasta with a pesto cream sauce. Definitely give this a try!
They were very easy and the flavor was good but they were very mushy. The meatballs were more of a blob than a ball.
I make these regularly for family dinners. Make them with garlic vermicelli!
I’ve made this probably 20x, sometimes I use shredded cheese because I don’t have cream cheese on hand. Turns out about the same! Love this lean recipe with some protein noodles!
Favor is wonderful!! The only change I made was used just 1 egg. Will definitely make again!!

These chicken meatballs were insanely good 😊 My husband is a very picky eater and he said, “Oh yeah these are GOOD!” Thanks so much for the recipe. Will definitely make these again! PS, I did use only 1 egg, extra breadcrumbs ( eyeballed, did not measure) and meatballs kept shape and were very moist.
These are amazing meatballs and versatile! We even loved them on subs!
